title: Socket controllers
summary: SocketRoute marks a controller class that keeps a WebSocket open, as Jakarta's @ServerEndpoint does. Tachyon makes one object of the class for each connection, so its fields hold that connection's state. OnOpen, OnMessage, OnClose and OnError mark the methods that run when a browser connects, sends a message, leaves, or when a method fails. Each message is JSON text, and Tachyon checks it against the model type of the OnMessage parameter first. The session sends messages back, and openSessions() (open_sessions() in Python, Ruby, Lua and Rust, OpenSessions() in Go, C# and F#, getOpenSessions() in Java) returns every open connection of the same path, so one message can go to every tab. In Go, session.Request() returns the request that opened the socket as an *http.Request, with the query string and the headers. When OnOpen or OnMessage fails, OnError runs and the socket stays open, as in Jakarta. In the browser, SocketRequest on an HTTPClient method receives the messages and publishes each one as its model's event, and the client's send(message) writes to the socket. The SocketRequest client is JavaScript, TypeScript, Go or Kotlin. A Go client is an interface method such as `Receive(message ChatMessage)`; the page holds the socket for the Go service that keeps the client in a `// @Needs` field, the service receives each message with `// @OnEvent`, and the generated `Send(message any) error` writes to the socket and returns an error code such as `HTTP_NETWORK` instead of a rejected promise. A Kotlin client is an interface method such as `fun receive(message: ChatMessage)`; the page holds the socket for the Kotlin web service that keeps the client in a `@Needs` field, and the generated `suspend fun send(message: Any)` waits for the page and throws an error whose message starts with the code, such as `HTTP_NETWORK`. Dart, Rust, Ruby, Python, Lua, Swift, Java, C#, F# and C++ refuse SocketRequest with TY1308, and their services receive the messages with OnEvent. Sockets are written in any Yon language. Tachyon guards every socket (ADR 0060): a message is JSON text of at most 64 KiB; a message that is not JSON or does not fit the model closes the socket with code 1007, a binary message with 1003, and a larger message with 1009. Five minutes without a message closes it with 1001, a socket lasts at most one hour, and a page from another origin gets 403. `Public`, `SignedIn` or `Allow(Role)` on the class says who may connect; Tachyon answers 401 or 403 before it opens the socket.
